questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: It usually happens when vehicles travel faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a lot of water for this to occur. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a suspension system defect?
questions.explanation: Check your suspension system for cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring, and leaking shock absorbers. Have any of these problems repaired right away.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, where should you drive?
questions.explanation: The right lanes are for slower traffic. If a heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. What happens if the air supply leaks away?

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank leaks, there are no working brakes and the wheels will spin freely.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
The weight of the tire itself.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a specific pressure.

questions.question: When can mirror adjustment be checked properly?

options.text: When the vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: On a vehicle with trailers, mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly when the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Cross the tracks before a train arrives.

questions.explanation: Always assume a train is coming. Do not rely on signals or sound to tell you if a train is there. Always slow down at a crossing. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: How do you prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?
questions.explanation: With manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal. This prevents the vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding?
questions.explanation: If your trailer is skidding, release the brakes to help your tires regain grip. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will only make it worse.

questions.question: In extremely hot weather, you may need to:

options.text: Drive faster to cool the engine.
Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.
Follow other vehicles closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.
questions.explanation: Driving faster creates more heat in the engine and tires. Slow down in very hot weather to avoid overheating.

questions.question: You should slow down and be extra careful:
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful in work zones, where the road edge drops off sharply, when objects are on the road, and on freeway entrance and exit ramps.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect is caused by:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification. Drivers should know the rearward amplification of their specific vehicles.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely right away while you can still control the brakes. Inspect and repair the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation that could happen.
Focus only on your own driving and not worry about other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation that could happen.
questions.explanation: While driving, check the road ahead for hazards. Make a plan to deal with any hazards you see coming.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers should be:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers or trailers without sides, all cargo must be tied down to keep it from moving or falling during transport.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
The weight of the tire itself.
The weight of the air inside a fully inflated tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the most weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. This information is printed on the tire's side.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: When a tire fails, you may hear a loud bang or feel heavy thumping or vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear starts to skid, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
Disconnecting air lines and listening for air escaping.
Removing and reattaching the rear shut-off valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure the air brake system supplies air to all trailers. Let air pressure build up, then send air to both emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: Avoid driving in fog if possible. If you must drive in foggy conditions, reduce your speed.
